name: Kiren Rijiju
role: Indian parliamentarian and union minister; Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs since 2024
summary: Rijiju advocates uniform civil law, national integration and state regulation of religious endowments. He supports trade and development partnerships, women’s legislative representation and preserving India’s regional languages, while defending deportation of unauthorized migrants.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He discusses legislative process without stating his preferred outcome.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His 2026 column calls preserving India’s linguistic and civilisational heritage a national responsibility.

reduce-immigration.rationale: His documented deportation policy addresses unauthorized entry; no clear position on reducing legal immigration levels was found.

free-trade.rationale: He welcomes India’s trade and investment partnership with Japan as beneficial to infrastructure and manufacturing.

nation-first.rationale: He says national interest is supreme and must precede all other considerations when defending the use of sedition law.

open-borders.rationale: His parliamentary answer defends the continuing detection and deportation of all illegal immigrants, including Rohingya.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He urges scientifically informed agricultural adaptation to serious climate impacts; this does not specify support for the statement’s drastic government action.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His Japan speech mentions civil nuclear cooperation without a clear prescription to expand nuclear generation.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He praises production-linked incentives and urges private manufacturers to meet India’s strategic need for domestically made weather radars.

algorithmic-government.rationale: He supports AI assistance in arbitration and paperless courts; these remarks do not advocate transferring government decision-making to algorithms.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: In his 2022 interview he explicitly advocates one common civil law to secure equality and composite nationhood.

restrict-conversion.rationale: In his 2013 interview he affirms the constitutional right to adopt a religion while defending the anti-conversion law and demanding checks on politicians’ involvement.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: He accepts cow-slaughter bans in Hindu-majority states but opposes imposing them on northeastern states with different food traditions.

population-transfer.rationale: He advocates relocating Chakma-Hajong refugees outside Arunachal Pradesh, while clarifying he did not propose Assam as the sole destination.

separated-powers.rationale: His parliamentary answer affirms distinct executive, legislative and judicial functions and constitutionally protected judicial independence.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He argues that Waqf receipts should serve poor beneficiaries rather than simply sustain the administering board. This evidence concerns charitable endowments.

death-penalty.rationale: He opposes abolishing capital punishment, while defending its restriction to exceptional cases and stressing appeals and clemency.

minority-language-support.rationale: He endorses promoting small-community languages, but the column does not specify their use in schools, public services or elections.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He personally drives greater civil regulation of Waqf property, including collector involvement and civil-court review, while distinguishing administration from religious practice.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He permits courts to overturn unconstitutional marriage laws.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: No stated position on equal or near-equal representation; a one-third reserved quota for women is something nearby.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He welcomes Japanese development loans supporting Indian power, transport, communications and northeastern connectivity.

single-official-language.rationale: He rejects replacing regional mother tongues with a common link language and demands equal respect for all Indian languages.

language-defines-nation.rationale: He describes linguistic diversity as foundational to Indian nationhood, with regional languages sharing one national heritage.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Defending the Waqf bill, he supports unifying Sunni, Shia and other Muslim sects under one board instead of separate sectarian boards.

women-suffrage.rationale: His advocacy of reserved legislative seats expressly supports women’s participation in elected public office.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: He defends excluding Chakma-Hajong refugees from permanent residence in Arunachal on the ground that it is a protected tribal state.

notes: No positions are inferred from BJP membership or ministerial portfolio. The July 2022 statement that UCC legislation was not yet planned concerns timing, rather than a withdrawal of his explicit personal endorsement. His 2024 Chakma-Hajong clarification still supports relocation outside Arunachal, while denying Assam as the sole destination. His 2026 language column is preferred for linguistic policy. A one-third women’s quota is scored as partial agreement with near-parity requirements. All 490 statements were reviewed; general climate concern, AI assistance and procedural marriage-law remarks are not expanded into stronger substantive positions.
